verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean states the same three components, never as this one display. Two independent encodings were opened. (a) Cartesian: AxisymmetricFields.potential H K is (rH/2) e_θ + K e_z, so the paper's Ψ is rH/2; with K = 0, velocity_zero/velocity_one give the vector (-x₀, -x₁) ∂_zH/2, which is purely radial (its e_θ component is identically 0, matching the middle entry) of radial size -(r/2)∂_zH = -∂_zΨ; velocity_two gives H + s ∂_sH with s = radialEnergy x = r²/2, and since ∂_r = r∂_s one has (∂_r + r⁻¹)(rH/2) = H + s∂_sH, the third entry. (b) Chart: meridional's body is literally the triple (-∂_zΨ, 0, ∂_rΨ + Ψ/r) written with graph derivatives (graphDz, graphDr with variable radial speed physicalSpeed) and divideRadius, and cartesianPotential_curl states that the Cartesian curl of the azimuthal potential equals its image under velocityMap/polarVelocityMap. In (b) the radius divided by is the chart radius p.1 = G.radialScale * r and graphDr carries the speed factor, so the identity is the paper's only after the chart scalings cancel; the cancellation inside velocityMap was not traced (see not_traced). No sign, derivative count or term differs in either encoding.
